title: Paraphrase and summarize a cactus passage
objective: Write one sentence in new words, then shorten a whole passage while keeping its main idea.
context: Class reading, adapted from the Week 5 summary worksheet: A cactus can live in dry places. Its thick stem stores water. A waxy layer on the stem helps keep water inside the plant. Spines help protect the cactus from animals that might eat it.

items.prompt: Paraphrase “Its thick stem stores water.” Keep both the plant part and its job.
items.answer: Example: The cactus keeps water in its thick stem. Give 1 mark for thick stem, 1 for water storage and 1 for a new sentence structure. Keep the term stem if useful.

items.prompt: Your summary will explain how a cactus saves water. Which two details do you need? Which detail can you leave out?
items.answer: 1 mark for stored water in the stem, 1 for the waxy layer reducing water loss, 1 for leaving out protection from animals.
items.hint: Which details answer the water question?

items.prompt: Write a one-sentence summary of how a cactus saves water. Aim for 12–20 words.
items.answer: Example: A cactus stores water in its stem, and a waxy cover helps it lose less water. Award 1 each for storage, reduced loss, a clear connection, and wording that preserves the meaning. Treat the word range as guidance.
items.hint: First make two short notes. Cover the passage and write from your notes.

slides.title: Try a new sentence
body: Source: The leaf has a smooth surface.
Possible paraphrase: The surface of the leaf is smooth.
Which words stayed because they name the parts?

slides.title: Work with the cactus passage
body: Tell a partner the job of the stem. Then write your own sentence.

slides.title: Choose what to keep
body: Your summary has one job: explain how the cactus saves water.
Choose the details that do this job.

slides.title: Check your summary
body: Can a reader find both ideas in the source?
Did you add a claim that the passage does not make?
